newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: VENDEX AIMS AT FURTHER SERVICES EXPANSION.
newsitem.headline: VENDEX AIMS AT FURTHER SERVICES EXPANSION.

text.p: Vedior, the services arm to be demerged from Dutch group Vendex later this year, aims for cross-border expansion in order to be able to compete for major international customers, board member Gert Smit said on Tuesday.
"In the field of services, we still have some way to go," Smit said at a results news conference. "We have only just started in Germany, where we are still relatively small."
"England is important in temporary employment as well, and we are not present over there at all for the moment," he said.
A major player has to be present in all big European countries in order to be able to offer major contracts, he said.
"This is valid for both cleaning and temporary employment."
Vendex has a 30 percent stake in Spanish temp agency Laborman, and intends to exercise call options to increase this stake first to 60 percent, and later to 100 percent, Smit said.
Laborman grew substantially in 1996, he said, with agencies increasing to 104 from 63, making it Spain's number two.
On January 6, Vendex announced plans to take over French temp employment agency BIS SA .
BIS posted a 106 million French franc loss for 1996, including a book loss of 215 million francs, down from a profit of 200 million francs the previous year.
When Vendex's take-over bid for BIS expired on March 21, the Dutch company held a 93.4 percent stake.
"Since then we've been offered another one percent of the shares. Every day, some BIS shares are handed over, and we're just under 95 percent at the moment," Smit said.
Smit said results of BIS had been positive during the first two months of 1997.
"We expect BIS to give a positive contribution to the group's results in 1997," Vendex's chairman Jan-Michiel Hessels said.
Retail and services group Vendex earlier on Tuesday announced a 30 percent rise in 1996/97 total net profit to 539 million guilders.
The services arm made an operating profit of 129 million guilders, up from 115 million in 1995/96. -- Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000, Fax +31 20 504 5040
